subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public API be nested/per-agent SSRF policy rather than the requested top-level `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes the SSRF boundary and current discussion rejects the first top-level shape without settling the final public contract.

options.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
options.body: Land a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache isolation, and redirect/metadata tests.

options.title: Add Global Broad Opt-In
options.body: Expose a simpler global private-network toggle and accept the larger blast radius with clear docs and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Reject Broad Private Access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or dedicated internal-service tools.

recommendation.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
recommendation.body: Land a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache isolation, and redirect/metadata tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible combination of recent SSRF/web_fetch history and prior review context on the rejected top-level shape.
